title: FormalJudge: A Neuro-Symbolic Paradigm for Agentic Oversight
evidence: judge: LLMs "handle only atomic semantic extraction" while Dafny specs + Z3 give the deterministic verdict (specs LLM-synthesized at runtime from user intent). judge_input RAW: extractor LLM(f_i, C(I,tau)) reads the trajectory incl. observations o_t; verifier "operates exclusively on grounded facts from actions and observations, ignoring explanations or reasoning traces". A_mode post: audits completed trajectory tau=(a_1,o_1,...,a_T,o_T); no inline pre-execution blocking found; refinement loop only feeds verdicts back so the agent regenerates (70.7%->99.8% over 3 rounds). adaptive 0: static attacks only (GPT-4.1 injects constraint violations into seed trajectories; Deceivers fault injection), no judge-aware optimization. Threat = agentic upward deception/fabrication (adversarial Y). n_models: 8 judge backbones (Claude-4.5-Opus, Qwen2.5 7/14/32/72B, + GPT-5.2/Grok-3/Gemini-2.5-Pro in appendix); 7 agent models judged; ground truth by LLM God-Judge ensemble. No task-success, latency/token/cost (only 180s Dafny/Z3 timeout), or FPR reported (accuracy/precision/recall only).

title: Learning When to Act or Refuse: Guarding Agentic Reasoning Models for Safe Multi-Step Tool Use
evidence: judge SELF: "refusal is optimized as part of the same action space as tool calls, rather than applied as a post-generation filter"; LLM-as-judge only compares trajectory pairs during GRPO training (reward), not at inference. A_mode pre: "plan, check, then act or refuse" loop with <safety_thoughts> before tool invocation, refusal_tool. judge_exposed Y: agent observation contains "tool responses, and environment feedback". adaptive 0: only existing static benchmarks (ASB, AgentHarm, Agent-SafetyBench injections); no adaptive/optimized attack. n_models: 3 fine-tuned (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507, Phi-4); GPT-4o and GPT-5 are un-trained baselines. utility: BFCLv3 +35% relative multi-turn accuracy; FPR: benign refusal Phi-4 0.43->0.19, Qwen2.5 0.13->0.15; token: safety reasoning below 20% of tokens. confirm: agent may "request user clarification or verification" but burden not measured.

title: IPIGuard: A Novel Tool Dependency Graph-Based Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
evidence: judge RULE: deterministic traversal of a planned Tool Dependency Graph with "strict constraints on tool invocations during execution"; "strictly prohibits access to tools not pre-approved in the plan". policy_src LLM: TDG built by the planning LLM whose input is only user instruction, tool descriptions and system context (no tool responses) -> judge_exposed N. Residual exposure: Node Expansion lets the LLM read tool responses but "only Query Tool invocations are allowed"; Fake Tool Invocation injects a simulated response to cover injected instructions (modify). A_mode pre: whole mechanism acts before action execution. adaptive 0: "Recent studies on adaptive IPI attacks (Zhan et al., 2025) demonstrate ..." cited as motivation only; attacks used = Ignore Previous, InjecAgent, Tool Knowledge (knows agent tools, not the defense), Important Instruction. Utility 67.01% vs 68.04% no defense; ASR avg 0.69%; GPT-4o-mini input tokens ~14.6k vs 6.2k, time 13.88s vs 7.13s. Models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-32B, o4-mini. No FPR/user confirmation.

title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
evidence: judge SEP: "we use the same model as a protective Task Shield" (separate LLM alignment check of each message). judge_input RAW: judge sees tool output with source annotation ("source: from tool [function_name] with arguments [args]") and original content, plus proposed tool calls "Function: {tool_name} Arguments: {tool_args}". A_mode pre: "prevents execution of misaligned calls"; assistant messages that fail get feedback; tool-output misalignment is flagged and "both the original output and feedback" are returned to the assistant (modify). Final natural-language answer checked only implicitly (no distinct output stage). adaptive 0: only Important Instructions, InjecAgent, Ignore Previous; no attacker aware of Task Shield; paper only notes "if the defender LLM is weak or adversarially probed, extraction or scoring may fail". Models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-3.5-turbo (appendix). utility GPT-4o 69.79% (ASR 2.07%), 4o-mini 54.53% (ASR 2.23%); latency median 62.56s full vs 6.17s no defense (Input Shield 18.78s). No FPR (only utility), no user confirmation.

title: Among Us: Measuring and Mitigating Malicious Contributions in Model Collaboration Systems
bench: own:malicious-LM collaboration setup over public datasets (CocoNot;SafetyBench;GSM8k;NLGraph;MMLU;TruthfulQA;HumanEval;DS-1000;IFBench;IFEval)
evidence: Model-collaboration (routing/debate), not tool-using agents. judge: supervisor-based = external "S1: LLM-as-a-judge or S2: reward model" (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B) that "evaluate the initial outputs of models and disable LMs with the lowest scores"; supervisor-free = top-k selection and "internal voting mechanism prior to collaboration, allowing models to collectively detect suspicious LLMs". judge_input RAW: other models raw responses (potentially malicious). Applied to API-level and text-level methods only; applied before integration of outputs (no A stage). adaptive 0: Limitations "may not fully capture more sophisticated or adaptive adversaries"; only a conditional-backdoor LLaMA-7B tested (not defense-aware). Malicious types: prompting, activation steering, SFT, RL. Recovery to 96.8% of initial performance on average (CocoNot ~89.2%). Overhead acknowledged but not quantified; no benign-model false-disable analysis. n_models: Qwen2.5-7B (5 fine-tuned + 1 malicious) main; heterogeneous test with 5 architectures (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Olmo-3-7B, Tulu-3-8B-DPO, Mistral-7B-v0.2). Public datasets are capability/safety QA sets, not agent-security benchmarks.

title: GUARDIAN: Safeguarding LLM Multi-Agent Collaborations with Temporal Graph Modeling
evidence: judge ML: non-LLM unsupervised GCN + Transformer temporal graph autoencoder over BERT embeddings of agent responses; anomaly if reconstruction error "s_v > tau" (learned thresholds); no LLM in detection. Online per round: "previously detected anomalous nodes removed" before the next round (prune anomalous agents/edges = limit/block); not an A-stage tool gate. Threat: adversary corrupts an agent response (prompt modification) or a communication edge. adaptive 0: "random" injection of 1 agent / edges, no defense-aware adversary, no limitation text on adaptivity. Public datasets are QA/capability sets, no security benchmark. Models: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-sonnet, Llama3.1-8B. Accuracy +4.2% avg over baselines (up to 7.1% on MATH); API calls lowest (e.g., 4.48 vs 8.00 on MMLU); detection rate 66.92-94.74% but no FPR/precision or no-attack utility.

title: VIGIL: Defending LLM Agents Against Tool-Stream Injection via Verify-Before-Commit
evidence: judge SEP: LLM roles - Intent Anchor (LLM constraints from user query only), Perception Sanitizer (LLM rewrite of tool docstrings/feedback), Speculative Reasoner, "role-specialized LLM" Grounding Verifier with V = Vcompliance AND Ventailment (both LLM-based). judge_input RAW because the sanitizer receives raw untrusted "tool docstrings, schemas" (D) and "status updates, error messages" (F) and removes "imperative commands"; the verifier itself gets only user query q, constraints C and candidate action metadata (DERIVED). A_mode pre: "synthesizing dynamic constraints anchored in user intent" before tool interaction; candidates explored in a hypothetical sandbox and verified before commit. Constraints are LLM-generated at runtime and enforced by an LLM verifier, not by a deterministic RULE. adaptive 0: black-box threat model; SIREN attacks are hand-crafted generic tool-stream vectors (Dependency Trap, Feature Inducement, Runtime Hijacking, Error Hijacking, Explicit Directive), "not generated through optimization loops" and not aimed at VIGIL; no adaptive section. Models: Qwen3-max, Gemini-2.5-pro, GPT-4o (App. D). Benign Utility 74.49% (Qwen3-max), 72.45% (GPT-4o) vs 79.59% vanilla ReAct. Overhead only Fig.4 verification rounds/time vs toolset scale (no tokens/cost); Limitations mention computational overhead. No FPR, no user confirmation.

title: SafeMCP: Proactive Power Regulation for LLM Agent Defense via Environment-Grounded Look-Ahead Reasoning
evidence: judge SEP: Qwen3-8B LLM-based reasoner (SFT + RL with verifiable rewards) as server-side MCP plugin with learned world model ("simulate-assess-constrain"; learned next-state prediction, no sandbox execution). A_mode pre: "proactive filtering layer prunes the tool set for step i+1" before the agent chooses, plus "immediate fail-safe tier blocks a_i" if the predicted state is unsafe. judge_input RAW: input is partial trajectory h_i incl. tool responses/execution results, state s_i and proposed call a_i, plus available tool set (so untrusted tool outputs enter the guard). Threat model non-adversarial (power-seeking, hallucination, no malicious MCP servers/injection) -> adversarial N, adaptive NA; no adaptive attacks. Models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-2.0-Flash, Llama-3.1-8B. Utility 0.22 with safety 0.99 on PowerSeeking Bench; over-blocking rate 0.01 (GPT-4o, AgentHarm); cost total $1.50 (-38.0% vs no guardrail), SafeMCP adds $0.022; latency unreported. Human study is annotator agreement (Cohen kappa), not user-confirmation burden.

title: AIR: Improving Agent Safety through Incident Response
evidence: judge SELF: "the agent itself" evaluates rule conditions - "natural-language description of the condition ... supplied to agent which uses it together with environment state, recent observations, and execution context"; rules (developer/LLM-authored, ANTLR4-parsed DSL with semantic NL checks) are not deterministic checks and no separate LLM is used (agent also synthesizes new guardrail rules). A_mode pre (hybrid): incident detection is post-execution ("After each step, AIR determines whether an incident has occurred") with containment/recovery, but guardrail rules "are evaluated right after the agent produces a plan ... AIR blocks the corresponding action before any tool invocation occurs" (first occurrence of a new incident only detected after execution). Threat model non-adversarial (accidental unsafe behavior; no attackers/adaptive discussion) -> adversarial N, adaptive NA. Single backbone: "All agents use OpenAI GPT-5". Detection >90%; safe-task completion reported (embodied 45/50, CUA 8/35, failures not caused by AIR); FPR 0 over ~85 safe tasks; latency: check 6.9-11.7s (0.16-0.68x of execution), 1.40-1.44x slowdown on safe tasks; no token/cost. Human-in-the-loop only recommended for validating LLM-generated rules, not part of the system.

title: ALRPHFS: Adversarially Learned Risk Patterns with Hierarchical Fast & Slow Reasoning for Robust Agent Defense
evidence: judge: fast thinking = embedding-based hybrid retrieval vs learned risk-pattern DB, "exceeds a predefined threshold ... directly triggers interception" (ML); slow thinking = LLM "risk verification function" for uncertain cases (SEP). A_mode pre: guards both queries and pending actions/plans/code "before execution" (low-risk reversible actions may be verified afterwards). judge_input RAW (inferred): slow-thinking prompt receives "< History > {history} </ History > < ACTION > ... < CONCERN >" i.e. the complete interaction history, which includes observations/tool outputs (paper does not state this explicitly). adaptive 0: red-blue "adversarial self-learning" (red team LLM gets EvaluateDefense outcomes and successful_attacks to generate next variants) is training-time pattern construction; final evaluation uses static test sets (R-Judge harmful split, ASB, TrustAgent, EICU-AC, Mind2Web-SC) and no adaptive attack against the final defense; no per-round ASR. Models: GPT-4o-mini and Claude-3.5-Haiku as defense backbone (GPT-4o only as offline red team). Avg accuracy 80%; TrustAgent ASR 28.57%/21.79%; FPR 19.24%/21.74% (TrustAgent); ~5000 tokens vs AGrail ~7000; no latency; no task-success utility; no human-in-the-loop.
